description:
Follow-on to v0.4 P3 (bl-829f). The shipped await detects \`stopped\`
via the §4.4 \`error\` event in the latest step's \`response.json\`.
The other stopped signature — kill mid-stream, ARCH §2.9 / §3.5,
where \`response.json\` is closed without \`message_stop\` and without
\`error\` — needs filesystem-close detection (\`IN_CLOSE_WRITE\`).

Scope:
- Wire an inotify watcher (or polling-mtime-stability fallback for
  non-Linux) into the await poll loop, so the subagent's latest
  response.json's close-without-terminal is detected and surfaced
  as \`{status: stopped}\`.
- Add the \`inotify\` crate (or equivalent) to the workspace deps.
  Mirror the UI's existing watcher dep choice (crates/lernie-ui-egui
  uses \`notify\` already — consider sharing).
- Tests: simulate a writer that opens response.json, writes a
  partial line, closes the fd; await resolves to \`stopped\`.

Out of scope:
- Re-architecting await's polling loop. The inotify watcher slots
  in as a parallel signal alongside the existing git-and-error
  poll; first signal to fire wins.

Why deferred from P3: the v0.4 minimal await ships \`error\` detection
(deterministic, single-poll) which covers the common provider-error
case; the kill case requires extra dependency and a separate test
shape. Filed per AGENTS.md "ship the milestone-correct part and
file the deferred piece".
title: await: detect killed-mid-stream subagents via filesystem-close (inotify)
